A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a healthful dietary pattern, as measured by multiple diet quality indices, is associated with lower risk of type 1 diabetes, independent of body mass index.

a diet high in fruits, vegetables, nuts, whole grains, fish, and poultry, with a low consumption of red and processed meats and sugary beverages, is associated with lower risk for T2D in postmenopausal white, African-American, Hispanic/Latina, and Asian-American women, and this association was independent of overweight/obesity.
a healthful diet, whether it be Mediterranean, DASH, or a diet that includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and fish, was associated with a lower incidence of diabetes.

there is no single diet that is optimal for everyone.
there are multiple healthful dietary patterns and all are associated with lower risk of diabetes.
